kpis.name: S&P 500
kpis.note: Broad equity risk-on/risk-off signal. High VIX or S&P drawdown signals demand risk for Southwire construction end markets.

kpis.name: Brent Crude
kpis.note: Energy costs affect Southwire manufacturing and logistics. Sustained Brent >$90 pressures freight and resin input costs.

kpis.name: Copper (LME)
kpis.note: Primary raw material. Copper content of wire drives COGS. Sustained elevation compresses margin unless hedged or repriced.

kpis.name: Aluminum (LME)
kpis.note: Key input for aluminum wire and cable. Price signals secondary cost pressure and hedge calendar triggers.

kpis.name: Freight (Drewry WCI)
kpis.note: Ocean freight index drives import costs on raw materials and packaging. WCI >$4K signals elevated supply chain risk.
kpis.change: Monitor Drewry WCI weekly for rate momentum

kpis.name: VIX
kpis.note: Equity market fear gauge. VIX >25 indicates risk-off environment; monitor customer demand signals and receivables.

kpis.name: Natural Gas
kpis.note: Energy input for manufacturing and logistics. Sustained elevation pressures margin. Drives residential heating demand indirectly.

kpis.name: Gold
kpis.note: Risk sentiment indicator. Gold >$3,000 with VIX elevation signals macro uncertainty that may dampen CapEx spending by customers.

wire.title: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks
wire.summary: The state's attorney general started investigating OpenAI after the Hugging Face attack and now says this attack was "entirely foreseeable" due to OpenAI's poor security practices.

wire.title: U.S. tightens controls on remote access to AI technology amid Nvidia fallout
wire.summary: The new rule closes a loophole that existed that allowed Chinese companies to still access advanced AI chips remotely, despite U.S. restrictions on their physical sale to China.

wire.title: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
wire.summary: Countries are meeting in Geneva to negotiate rules on weapons that can select and kill targets without human intervention. But with the U.S., Russia and Israel resisting legally binding controls, campaigners fear the window to act is closing.

wire.title: Nearly two million people are behind bars in the US. How did we get here?
wire.summary: Lynn Novick's new, four-part PBS documentary series, Crime and Punishment in America , goes inside the U.S. prison system and explores how our approach to criminals has changed over time.

wire.title: Lindsay Clancy to face a new trial in spring of 2027 over children's killing
wire.summary: A new trial is set in Massachusetts against Lindsay Clancy as prosecutors seek a criminal conviction over the killing of her three young children.

wire.title: FAA ground stop still affecting thousands of flights. And, Trump meets Xi, Putin in Asia
wire.summary: U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that things could be back to normal at the end of Monday after an FAA ground stop disrupted flights. And, Trump heads to Asia for a high-profile trilateral summit.

wire.title: Chris Van Hollen says he can beat Chuck Schumer. Here's his case
wire.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen told NPR's Morning Edition why he believes he can defeat Sen. Chuck Schumer and what he would change about Senate Democratic leadership.

wire.title: Regulating AI will being a top priority for congressional Democrats in the new year
wire.summary: A big priority for the incoming Congress will be regulating artificial intelligence. Democrats will face stiff opposition from the Trump administration and its hands-off policy towards AI.

wire.title: These birds fly 17,000 miles every year. Climate change could make it harder
wire.summary: Migratory birds cross the entire globe, carefully timing their journeys with the seasons. In a hotter climate, that timing is increasingly out of sync.

wire.title: NPR's Student Podcast Challenge is back for 2027
wire.summary: The annual audio competition for grades four through 12 returns in January. Now in its ninth year, the contest has involved more than 90,000 students around the country.

wire.title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
wire.summary: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have announced a "return hub" for failed asylum seekers.

wire.title: Houthi rebel advance in Yemen may further destabilise global economy
wire.summary: The Iran-backed Houthis are gaining ground and their advance could have dangerous consequences, writes the BBC's security correspondent.

wire.title: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex CEO
wire.summary: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.

wire.title: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war
wire.summary: Russia said Ukraine had launched over 2,000 drones over the course of a day, while Kyiv came under a record 17 air raid alerts.

wire.title: When will we see Robert Pattinson as Bond in cinemas?
wire.summary: Robert Pattinson has been announced as the next James Bond, becoming the seventh actor to take up the mantle of 007.

wire.title: Forensic expert says his analysis of autopsy photos suggests Epstein was killed
wire.summary: Professor Michael Freeman tells BBC Newsnight that he believes the convicted sex offender's injuries are consistent with a homicide.
